identity.name: Collection and Data-Staging Behavioral Anomaly — Cortex ABIOC (T1074.001 / T1560.001 / T1005)
identity.summary: A service process whose learned Cortex profile never reads bulk files or writes archives performs a bulk file-read sweep then an archive/compression staging burst — the pre-exfil collection tradecraft attributed to Scattered Spider. The deviation from the learned baseline plus the causality chain is what the auto-tuned ABIOC fires on.
identity.description: Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) is a first-party Cortex detection type distinct from a hand-authored BIOC: PANW authors and continually tunes ABIOCs against the user, endpoint, and process behavioral profiles Cortex learns per environment, firing on a single suspicious event that carries an identified chain of causality. This scenario exercises that detector class on the ENDPOINT plane for the collection/staging kill-chain phase — the pre-exfil moment where an intruder gathers and compresses data before it leaves the estate. It models the signature staging tradecraft attributed to Scattered Spider / Muddled Libra (UNC3944) and observed in Mandiant-tracked extortion intrusions: after obtaining access, the operator sweeps local files, concentrates them into a staging directory, and compresses them into a single archive so the subsequent exfil is one clean transfer. Cortex has learned that the acting process (a web/app service identity such as www-data) exhibits a narrow, stable behavioral profile — it serves requests and touches a bounded set of files, and it never fans out reads across the filesystem nor spawns tar/gzip/zip to produce archives. The scenario injects two behavioral deviations from that learned baseline: (a) a bulk file-read sweep whose read count and file-diversity exceed the process's learned baseline, and (b) an archive/compression staging burst (tar -czf / gzip) that the process has never performed. A hand-authored BIOC keyed on a specific bad binary or path would miss this — tar, gzip, and cat are legitimate on every host — which is exactly the point: the auto-tuned ABIOC fires on the deviation from the process's learned behavior and anchors it to the causality chain (service process -> bulk read sweep -> archive creation in a staging directory). Two ABIOCs cover the two deviation shapes; supporting validation XQL confirms the learned baseline and surfaces the staging deviation; a correlation rule stitches the two ABIOCs into a single collection-and-staging (pre-exfil) incident the DC presents as proof that Cortex's behavioral analytics caught novel activity no static rule was written for.

campaigns: Data-theft and extortion intrusions with local staging prior to bulk exfiltration (2023-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-012 — Collection/staging behavioral deviation on a learned service process for Cortex ABIOC validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM Linux agent installed on the target host so per-process, command, and file-access telemetry reaches xdr_data.
A baseline window has elapsed during which the acting service process (www-data) performed only its normal request-serving workload so Cortex learned its non-staging behavioral profile.

payload.code:
# No known-bad payloads. Drive a learned service process to sweep local files and
# stage them into a single archive, deviating from its non-staging baseline.
set -euo pipefail
stage=/tmp/cortexsim-collect
mkdir -p "$stage"
# (a) bulk file-read sweep exceeding the process's learned read diversity
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do dd if=/dev/urandom of="$stage/doc-$i.dat" bs=1k count=8 2>/dev/null; done
cat "$stage"/doc-1.dat "$stage"/doc-2.dat "$stage"/doc-3.dat >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# (b) archive/compression staging burst the process has never performed
tar -czf /tmp/cortexsim-stage.tar.gz "$stage" 2>/dev/null || true
gzip -k "$stage/doc-1.dat" 2>/dev/null || true

input_variables.name: STAGE_DIR
input_variables.description: Authorised local staging directory the collection sweep and archive burst use during the deviation.

expected_artifacts.description: An archive/compression process (tar or gzip) spawned by a service process whose learned baseline never produces archives.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: actor_effective_username = "www-data" and action_process_image_name in (tar, gzip, zip)

expected_artifacts.description: A staging archive written under a temp/staging directory concentrating swept files ahead of exfiltration.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: action_file_path contains "cortexsim-stage" and action_file_extension in (gz, tar, zip)

abiocs.name: EDR-012 Anomalous Bulk File-Read Sweep from Non-Staging Process
abiocs.description: A service process whose learned Cortex behavioral profile touches a narrow, stable set of files suddenly reads a fan-out of distinct files across the filesystem. ABIOC anchors the read-count-and-diversity deviation to the causality chain (service process -> bulk read sweep) rather than to any known-bad path, catching pre-exfil collection that a static rule keyed on a bad file or binary would miss.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type = ENUM.FILE_OPEN
| filter actor_effective_username in ("www-data", "node", "nobody")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "node")
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("cat", "dd", "cp", "tar", "find")
| comp count_distinct(action_file_path) as distinct_files, values(actor_process_instance_id) as proc_instances by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter distinct_files >= 5
| sort desc distinct_files
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, distinct_files, proc_instances
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned non-staging process baseline (bounded file set, no bulk reads) -> service CGO (causality_actor_process_image_name = apache2/httpd/nginx, effective user www-data) -> bulk file-read sweep whose file diversity exceeds the learned baseline, keyed on the causality_actor and actor_process_instance_id rather than any known-bad path.

abiocs.name: EDR-012 Archive/Compression Staging Burst Deviating from Process Baseline
abiocs.description: A service process whose learned baseline never produces archives spawns tar/gzip/zip to compress swept files into a single staging artifact. Every utility is legitimate; the ABIOC fires on the archive-creation deviation from the process's learned behavior, anchored to the bulk-read sweep that fed it — the pre-exfil staging moment.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_effective_username in ("www-data", "node", "nobody")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "node")
| filter action_process_image_name in ("tar", "gzip", "zip", "7z", "xz", "bzip2")
| filter action_process_command_line contains "-c" or action_process_command_line contains "tmp"
| comp count() as archive_ops, values(actor_process_instance_id) as proc_instances by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_name
| filter archive_ops >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_name, archive_ops, proc_instances
abiocs.causality_anchor: Bulk file-read sweep under the service CGO (causality_actor_process_image_name = apache2/httpd/nginx) -> archive/compression process (tar/gzip) writing a staging artifact the process has never produced, keyed on the shared causality_actor and actor_process_instance_id that fed the archive.

xql_queries.name: EDR-012 Service Process Non-Staging Baseline Learned
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 600)
| filter actor_effective_username = "www-data"
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as baseline_tools by agent_hostname
| filter baseline_tools >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, baseline_tools

xql_queries.name: EDR-012 Staging Deviation Surfaced on Process Baseline
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 600)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_effective_username = "www-data"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("tar", "gzip", "zip")
| comp count() as staging_ops by agent_hostname
| filter staging_ops >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, staging_ops

correlation_rules.name: Collection and Data-Staging Intrusion on Service Process — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(EDR-012 Anomalous Bulk File-Read Sweep from Non-Staging Process) AND ABIOC(EDR-012 Archive/Compression Staging Burst Deviating from Process Baseline) — fuses the two auto-tuned behavioral deviations on the same host+process into a single collection-and-staging (pre-exfil) incident anchored to the read-sweep-to-archive causality chain.

use_cases.name: Collection and Data-Staging Behavioral Anomaly Detection via Cortex ABIOC
use_cases.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn a service process's non-staging baseline and detect pre-exfil collection and archive staging by that process, anchored to its causality chain, where no static rule was written for the legitimate archive utilities involved.

test_cases.objective: Cortex learns the www-data non-staging baseline and an injected collection/staging deviation fires both ABIOCs.
preconditions: EDR target with the Cortex Linux agent installed.
Baseline window elapsed with www-data serving only its normal workload.
steps: Let the process baseline window elapse.
Run a bulk file-read sweep then an archive/compression staging burst under www-data.
Observe both ABIOCs fire and CR-EDR-0012 raise a collection-and-staging incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `EDR-012 Anomalous Bulk File-Read Sweep from Non-Staging Process` fires.
ABIOC `EDR-012 Archive/Compression Staging Burst Deviating from Process Baseline` fires.
Correlation CR-EDR-0012 raises one stitched collection-and-staging (pre-exfil) incident.

preventive_controls: Constrain service accounts with filesystem allow-lists (AppArmor/SELinux) so a web/app identity cannot read outside its served content tree or write archives to temp directories.
Enforce egress controls and DLP so a staged archive cannot be transferred even if it is created.
Scope and rotate service-account credentials tightly to shrink the blast radius of the initial access Scattered Spider abuses.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-process file-access and archive-creation baseline rather than hand-authoring static rules for individual archive utilities.
Alert on a service process reading a file-diversity that exceeds its learned baseline.
Alert on a service process spawning archive/compression utilities its baseline has never produced.
